title: Annotatio IV §.XII: Orthodox opposition — Constantinople; FIGURE OF CHRIST’S BODY vs all images
pass_a_gloss: Meanwhile, Damascene and very many followers thus wandering from the manifold truth, in the same Eighth age not a few truly Orthodox — i.e. those clinging more closely to Holy Scripture — opposed themselves to the flood of errors about to inundate the universal Church, when stirred from their seats on every side they gathered at Constantinople a Council called from this City the fifth, by the Greeks said to be the seventh Oecumenical, under Constantine Copronymus and Leo the Isaurian, vindicated by our Spanheim from varied fame and the wanton laceration of their reputation; These, by the FIGURE OF CHRIST’S BODY which they set in the Supper, were trying to abrogate and remove from the midst every sacred use of figures or of all Images,
pass_b_english: Meanwhile truly Orthodox (Scripture-clinging) opposed Damascene’s flood of errors in the same Eighth age.

Gathered at Constantinople (fifth / Greeks’ seventh Oecumenical; Copronymus and Leo Isaurian — Spanheim vindicates them): by the FIGURE OF CHRIST’S BODY they set in the Supper they tried to abolish every sacred use of images.
source_text: Intereà deviantibus ita à veritate multijuga, Damasceno & asseclis quàm plurimis, eodem seculo Octavo, errorum flumini, universam Ecclesiam inundaturo, sese opposuere verè Orthodoxi, i. e. Scripturæ S. pressius inhærentes haud pauci, dum sedibus suis undique exciti, Constantinopolim convenerunt Concilium, ab hac Civitate denominatum quintum, Græcis Oecumenicum septimum dictum, sub Constant. Copronymo & Leone Isaurico, à varia fama & æstimationis suæ proterva laceratione per Spanhemium nostrum vindicatis, celebratum; Hi per FIGURAM CORPORIS CHRISTI quam in Cœna statuebant, omnem figurarum seu Imaginum omnium usum sacrum abrogare éque medio tollere conabantur,
